newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends thin bourse trade at four week low.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends thin bourse trade at four week low.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares on Thursday ended thin-volume bourse trade at its lowest level in four weeks as the possibility of further German interest rate cuts faded and Wall Street closed lower.

German rate cut hopes were knocked on Wednesday, when Britain announced a rise in its base interest rate, but the move came just before the close of floor dealings and the market did not have time to react fully.
The DAX index closed floor dealings down 19.48 points, or 0.73 percent, at 2,659.25.

Overall, dealers said the market tone was mixed, with interest mainly focused on individual stocks and said the market was cautious ahead of important U.S. data due out later in the day and on Friday.
Meanwhile the banking sector was the main centre of attention as nine month results were released.

Dresdner Bank, which had risen in IBIS dealings after it said its operating profits rose 29.7 percent to 1.89 billion marks for the first nine months of the year, ended bourse trade down 50 pfennigs at 40.50 marks.
Dealers said the results had been mainly in line with expectations, although analysts expressed surprise at a 14.8 decline in own-account trading profits to 456.2 million marks in the period.
The day's biggest gainer was engineering firm Deutsche Babcock, which has been suffering from rumours it was facing insolvency, categorically denied by the company.

The stock ended bourse trade up 3.20 marks, or eight percent, at 43.20 marks after Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale, which holds 10 percent of the company, said its restructuring programme would be a sucess.

Shares in business software compnay SAP AG fell on continued worries about the former market favourite, after it issued a profit warning last week. Preference shares in the company, listed on the DAX, ended down 8.40 marks, or nearly four percent, at 203.80 marks.
